body:
`insight:flag-losses-dilution-context` · verified

RULE (LOSSES): losses are benign when (1) unit economics are already positive (contribution margin per order/customer/store) and the losses are growth spending or a new segment (Eternal 2022-23; Amazon 1997-2002); (2) the loss is one-time and non-operating (Bharti FY20-21 AGR provision Rs 28,450 cr in one quarter while CFO stayed strong); (3) losses are investee/mark-to-market items around a profitable core (Info Edge). Losses are real when unit economics are negative and worsen with scale, when cash burn needs ever-larger raises, or when the 'path to profit' depends on competitors leaving. RULE (DILUTION): judge by price x purpose x buyer x per-share outcome. Benign: raising at high valuation for high-return growth, ideally small in % terms (Tesla 2020: $12 bn at ~$500 bn, ~1% per raise; Bajaj Finance QIPs at 5-8x book with EPS still up 17x FY15-26; Eternal's Rs 8,500 cr QIP at Rs 252.62 from domestic MFs); rights issues the promoter fully subscribes (Bharti 2019, Reliance 2020). Malignant: equity raised at depressed prices to survive, preferential allotments/warrants to obscure entities, convertible death spirals, heavy SBC (insight:us-redflag-sbc-dilution), or promoter selling into the raise. TEST: per-share metrics net of dilution (EPS, BVPS, FCF/share, 5-year diluted share count CAGR); who bought; use of proceeds vs subsequent capex/ROCE.

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:TATAPOWER:fy27-capacity-addition-2-5gw`
- **Method:** sector cycle/lead indicator · **P(ours)** 0.30 · **P(base)** 0.40 · resolve by 2027-05-31
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (11-Nov-2026): CEO Praveer Sinha: 'we have missed the targets in first and second quarter, but many of the projects are now ready. The evacuation lines which were delayed, we are expecting some of them to come by December or January… this year target is 2.5 GW of capacity addition, and we will be able to meet that.' NTPC's call the same month also cites transmission (evacuation) delays leaving ~1.5 GW stranded (sector-wide lead indicator).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Lead indicator: transmission/evacuation delays are sector-wide and outside the developer's control; H1 shortfall means H2 must carry most of 2.5 GW. Promise reaffirmation after two misses is weak evidence.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Indian RE developers meet annual commissioning targets after a behind-plan H1 roughly 40% of the time.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Tata Power's Q4 FY27 results presentation/press release states renewable (utility-scale + group captive, as Tata Power itself counts it) capacity commissioned/added during FY27 ≥2.5 GW (2,500 MW). Rooftop/distributed solar excluded unless Tata Power includes it in the same 2.5 GW target definition.
- **Resolution source:** Tata Power Q4 FY27 investor presentation / press release
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/KSTPCL_17112026152929_Q2_FY27_Earning_Call_Transcript.pdf; https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/9425178051_06112026150753_6__Disclosure_for_Transcript_of_Earnings_Conference_Call_Q2_FY27_Signed.pdf

- E: dead firms are a 39% sample with returns run to their last traded close (survivorship check convention).
  A firm whose price series stops inside a window is scored on what traded; a window cut short only because the
  *data* end (series last close within 14 days of the cache's latest date) is censored and dropped from that
  outcome (counted). 3-year outcomes therefore use entries up to ~Nov-2023 only.
- P: census of dead/distress firms with sampling weights; outcomes from screener weekly prices + IBBI/NSE/BSE lists,
  exactly as in the solvency test (`panel.csv`). Prices for 1-year halving and 1y/3y returns from the same cached
  screener charts (`bt_solv_in/sc/<slug>/chart.json`).
